caption_raw: 1,656 likes, 56 comments - theartificialintelligence on July 19, 2026: "Kimi AI just did something you almost never see a company do: it stopped taking people's money.  Moonshot AI paused new subscriptions after demand for Kimi K3 — its new 2.8-trillion-parameter flagship launched on July 16 — pushed its computing capacity to the edge. Users reported outages and paused tasks within a day of launch, and the company chose to protect existing subscribers rather than oversell access it couldn't serve.  Here's the part worth sitting with: K3 is being compared to the best closed models from OpenAI and Anthropic, and Moonshot built it under US chip export restrictions. The model isn't the bottleneck anymore. Compute is. A company with over $200M in annual recurring revenue and billions in funding still can't buy enough chips to meet demand.  That's the real story of the AI race in 2026 — talent and research are spreading everywhere, but access to hardware decides who gets to serve customers.  Subscriptions are expected to reopen as capacity scales. The model's full weights are also set to go open source by end of July, which means the demand problem may only get bigger.  Follow @theartificialintelligence for daily AI news that actually matters.  #KimiAI #KimiK3 #MoonshotAI #ArtificialIntelligence #AInews".
